issue: Can a federal court toll a defendant's term of supervised release while he is a fugitive from supervision, so that the court keeps jurisdiction to revoke it for violations committed after the scheduled expiration date?

sides.position: Fugitive tolling applies: absconding from supervision equitably tolls the supervised release term for the period of truancy.
cases: United States v. Island, 916 F.3d 249 (3d Cir. 2019)
United States v. Barinas, 865 F.3d 99 (2d Cir. 2017)
United States v. Buchanan, 638 F.3d 448 (4th Cir. 2011)
United States v. Murguia-Oliveros, 421 F.3d 951 (9th Cir. 2005)

sides.position: No fugitive tolling: there can be no tolling of the supervised release period on the basis of fugitive status.
cases: United States v. Hernandez-Ferrer, 599 F.3d 63 (1st Cir. 2010)
United States v. Talley, 83 F.4th 1296 (11th Cir. 2023)

this_court: No fugitive tolling; the court joins the First Circuit and holds the term of supervised release is not tolled by fugitive status.
quote: The circuits are divided over the application of “fugitive tolling” to terms of supervised release.
cite: United States v. James Reginald Talley, 83 F.4th 1296 (11th Cir. 2023)
